entries.title: Try an interactive block before your next presentation
entries.summary: Pitch introduced the Agent-powered Anything block for prompted slide elements such as calculators and tabbed views, using the presentation theme's colors and fonts.
entries.action: Prototype with non-sensitive sample data. Verify calculations, keyboard access, and behavior in the exact sharing or export format your audience will use; do not assume interactions survive a static export. Check current access and usage terms.

entries.title: Hand off tables that recipients can still edit
entries.summary: Gamma's August release notes describe editable tables in PowerPoint exports and in Google Slides after upload, with an opt-out when visual fidelity matters more. This is an earlier release newly tracked here.
entries.action: Export a sample deck and open it in the recipient's app. Check table values, wrapping, fonts, and editability before delivery; retain a reviewed PDF reference and confirm permissions for client data and images.

entries.title: Check grammar in Korean and other added languages
entries.summary: Grammarly's March announcement added beta grammar and spelling support for languages including Korean through its browser extension and desktop app. The announcement treated advanced tone and clarity suggestions as future work, not part of that release.
entries.action: Check current support in your app with a short, non-sensitive draft. Review names, numbers, politeness, and intended commitments yourself; a grammar correction does not verify facts or guarantee appropriate tone. This March release is newly tracked, not an October launch.

entries.title: Check whether a citation supports your claim
entries.summary: Consensus introduced Skills in Deep mode, including Verify Citations: a workflow that compares a draft's claims with cited sources and shows passages behind its assessment.
entries.action: Start with one non-sensitive section. Read the original paper and check its methods, population, and context before accepting a verdict. Follow academic disclosure rules; an AI citation check is not proof of accuracy.

entries.title: Keep an evidence review current with Routines
entries.summary: Elicit introduced Routines for recurring Research Agent work, including finding new evidence and preparing an updated artifact for review. Instructions and schedules can be edited before activation.
entries.action: Define the research question and inclusion criteria first. Inspect original papers and citations before changing conclusions, check current usage terms, and keep confidential material out unless your policy permits it. Monitoring does not guarantee complete coverage.

entries.title: Connect source summaries with quizzes and flashcards
entries.summary: Google's Gemini Notebook announcement describes a rollout of interactive learning overviews combining summaries with study outputs such as quizzes and flashcards. Check availability in your account rather than assuming the rollout is complete.
entries.action: Use material you are allowed to upload, try answering without notes, and check generated answers against the original sources. Correct misleading questions before sharing, follow academic rules, and avoid uploading sensitive documents without approval.
entries.sourceTitle: Google: New Gemini Notebook study tools

entries.title: Describe scenario versions before changing an automation
entries.summary: Make's updated toolbar adds descriptions to saved scenario versions and displays them in version history, helping users choose a version to restore.
entries.action: Save a named baseline before editing. Test with sample data and inspect activation settings before resuming; restoring a scenario does not undo emails already sent or records already changed.
entries.sourceTitle: Make: Improved scenario toolbar and version control

entries.title: Prioritize workflow fixes before an n8n upgrade
entries.summary: n8n 2.43 release notes describe clearer migration-report impact categories and a progress summary of workflows compatible with the target version.
entries.action: Check availability on your instance, back up configuration, and test affected workflows in staging. Start with upgrade blockers and execution failures; a compatible label is not a substitute for testing real inputs.

entries.title: Evaluate Next Gen Zaps without replacing live workflows
entries.summary: Zapier announced early access to Next Gen Zaps, including branches that rejoin and runs that pause for a human reply. Access is requested rather than assumed available to every account.
entries.action: Confirm eligibility and billing before trying a small workflow. Test approval pauses, error paths, and duplicate handling with non-production accounts before migrating a working Zap.

entries.title: Turn a repeated team task into a shared skill
entries.summary: Notion 3.7 introduced a shared library of reusable agent instructions for tasks such as document review and business briefs. This September announcement is newly tracked here.
entries.action: Start with one task, an approved example, and a named owner. Test outputs and sharing permissions, remove sensitive examples, and recheck exported copies when the original skill changes.

entries.title: Use LM Studio for Bionic's local inference
entries.summary: LM Studio 0.4.26 lists coexistence with Bionic: while both apps run, Bionic can use LM Studio for local model inference. The note requires Bionic 1.1.8 or newer.
entries.action: Check both installed versions and the selected model endpoint. Test a small task and monitor memory use; local inference alone does not mean connected tools or every part of an agent workflow stay offline.

entries.title: Distinguish Ollama's new cloud connector from local use
entries.summary: Ollama announced a connector for using its cloud models inside Fly.io Sprites. This is a cloud execution option, not an update that makes those models run on your laptop.
entries.action: Before connecting, check both services' costs, data policies, and which Sprites have access. Start with non-sensitive input and minimum permissions; do not assume a cloud sandbox guarantees confidentiality.

entries.title: Test a video idea in Draft mode before finishing
entries.summary: Runway's October 2 release adds Seedance 2.5 Draft mode in Agent, with lower-resolution drafts and post-generation enhancement.
entries.action: Use a short draft to check composition and motion before finishing. Verify credit costs and output settings, then inspect product details, text, likenesses, and media rights again in the final video.

entries.title: Guide image edits with markup and variation controls
entries.summary: Previously announced in April: Adobe introduced AI Markup for visually targeted edits and Precision Flow in beta for exploring image variations. This is newly tracked here, not a new October launch.
entries.action: Try an owned image and compare edited areas with the original. Check current access and beta status, inspect unintended changes to logos or products, and confirm rights before client delivery.
entries.sourceTitle: Adobe: April 9 Firefly image editing announcement

entries.title: Review agent edits and database access in Notion
entries.summary: Notion 3.8 announces clearer page and database change history with attribution, plus database column permissions for people and agents.
entries.action: Before connecting a team agent, test access with a low-privilege account and inspect its edits. Check your plan and retention options; visible history is not a substitute for a backup or permission audit.
entries.sourceTitle: Notion: October 13 release, Context for your agents

entries.title: Review Claude's policy update before November 12
entries.summary: Anthropic announced a revised Usage Policy taking effect November 12, 2026. It clarifies existing high-risk-use requirements and adds requirements for autonomous physical actions.
entries.action: Teams using Claude for consequential decisions should read the full policy and confirm qualified human oversight and disclosure. This is a forthcoming vendor-policy update, not legal advice or a new permission to automate decisions.

entries.title: Explore file data with charts inside Computer
entries.summary: Perplexity's October release describes interactive visualizations directly in Computer threads, including turning a CSV file into an interactive chart.
entries.action: Try a small, non-sensitive file first. Check totals, units, missing values, and source dates against the original data before using a chart in a report; confirm access and usage costs in your account.

entries.title: Work across existing projects from one chat
entries.summary: Replit says a chat can find projects, read their files, and send background tasks for review. Its announcement says these changes are not published automatically.
entries.action: Confirm the source and destination projects before sending work. Review permissions, copied code, and each diff; test the destination app before publishing.

entries.title: Check local agent sandbox permissions
entries.summary: GitHub announced local sandboxing for Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host. Policies can restrict file, network, and credential access.
entries.action: Check support and active policy in your client before use. Test with a disposable repository and limit permissions; sandboxing does not replace code review or protect every secret automatically.

entries.title: Follow local agents from the Cursor iOS app
entries.summary: Cursor announced remote viewing and replies for local agents through its iOS app. The agent stays on your computer, which must remain on and online.
entries.action: Review device pairing and workplace policy before enabling access. Cursor says remote control defaults on outside Enterprise organizations; check your settings and keep reviewing changes before release.
entries.sourceTitle: Cursor: Remote control for local agents

entries.title: Check model replacements before October 19
entries.summary: GitHub's September announcement schedules selected Copilot models for retirement on October 19, 2026. The notice lists affected models and suggested replacements.
entries.action: Compare your model choices with the official list and test a supported replacement on a familiar task. Check organization model policies; this is a scheduled change, not a claim that retirement has already happened.

entries.title: Review comments can close after a follow-up commit
entries.summary: GitHub reports that Copilot can resolve its own addressed review comments during a rereview, alongside changes to review analysis.
entries.action: Inspect the actual diff and test results before merging. A resolved AI comment is not evidence that a fix is correct.

entries.title: Desktop MCP clients can connect to Replit
entries.summary: Replit's release note describes connecting compatible desktop MCP clients to work with apps, including publishing actions.
entries.action: Review the connected account, exposed actions, and approval settings. Start with a disposable app before allowing changes to production work.

entries.title: Projects introduces coordinated, longer-running work
entries.summary: Cursor announced a beta rollout of Projects, with a coordinator delegating work to agents and maintaining shared project context.
entries.action: Check rollout access, execution locations, connected services, and how to stop work before testing. Keep secrets out of shared context and review each resulting change.
